title: A Comprehensive Survey on LLM-Guided Evolutionary Search
content: Large Language Model-guided Evolutionary Search (LLM-ES), exemplified by AlphaEvolve, has recently demonstrated impressive performance in solving goal-driven problems with extremely large and complex search spaces. Unlike conventional LLM approaches based on single-shot or few-shot sampling, LLM-ES introduces population-based evolution to iteratively generate more novel and higher-quality solutions. Compared with traditional Evolutionary Computing algorithms, LLM-ES treats LLMs as semantic variation operators. This design extends the search space from low-dimensional vectors to expressive and language-defined structures such as code and programs. Meanwhile, the rich prior knowledge embedded in LLMs significantly improves the efficiency of evolutionary search in complex solution spaces. As a result, LLM-ES effectively exploits the test-time scaling capability of LLMs and achieves state-of-the-art performance in many open-ended problems. In this survey, we provide a systematic overview of this emerging field. We first formalize the problem setting and the general pipeline of LLM-ES. We then review existing works from several key perspectives, including population design, prompt builder, LLM model selection, evaluation design, and exploration-exploitation control. Finally, we summarize representative applications and discuss open challenges and future research directions.
